The dictionary cites Dudasova, Prochazka, Vaculik & Lorenz (2021) PLOS ONE 16(3):e0247114 (CC BY 4.0), whose subject is the CPC-12/CPC-12R psychological-capital scale. The words "engagement", "UWES", "Utrecht" and "Schaufeli" occur ZERO times in the full article text (253KB HTML scraped and de-tagged; 64.5KB of text). Its two Measures sections describe only the CPC-12 (Study 1) and CPC-12R (Study 3); the Study 1 Participants-and-procedure paragraph says only "The survey was conducted in Czech" and names no other instrument. The engagement block is one of nine unmentioned scales carried in the S1 deposit (Eng, JS, LifeSat, Hope, SocSup, Grat, PosAff, Perf, CWB) that the paper never describes. (2) THE DEPOSIT CARRIES NO LABELS. All four .sav supplements were downloaded and read with pyreadstat: S1 (.s001, 282x103) has exactly 2 labelled columns, both SPSS artefacts ("REGR factor score 1/2 for analysis 1"), and Eng1-Eng9 carry no variable label; S2 (.s002, 321x12) and S3 (.s003, 202x12) have 0 labelled columns; S4 (.s004, 338x88) has 1 ("Res1-no"). NOT ONE of the four files has a single value-label set (variable_value_labels empty in all four), so neither the item stems nor the 1-7 anchors are recoverable from the data. The only appendix, S1 Appendix (.s005, DOCX), is titled "CPC-12R in Czech and English" and covers the CPC-12R alone. data/dudasova_2021_cpc12_battery.py carries the source column names Eng1..Eng9 through a plain melt unchanged, so the item codes are the .sav headers and are the only description of the items that exists. (3) THE INSTRUMENT IS NOT EVEN IDENTIFIED. The IRW dictionary Description ("Work engagement scale (UWES-9-style, 9 items)") is an IRW conjecture, not a source claim. It is weakly consistent with the data and no more: 9 items, and the canonical UWES-9 facet assignment (vigour 1,2,5 / dedication 3,4,7 / absorption 6,8,9) gives mean within-facet r = 0.593 vs between-facet r = 0.494 with only 6 of 9 items finding their strongest partner inside their own facet (Eng5 pairs with Eng3, Eng6 with Eng7) -- the same underpowered 6/9 that algner2022_uwes produced, because UWES facets are collinear. The live resp set is 1-7, whereas the published UWES scale is 0-6; a recode is plausible but unevidenced. The same team's only other paper on this teacher cohort (Dudasova, Prochazka & Vaculik 2024, Current Psychology 10.1007/s12144-024-05841-9, spring-2019 wave, n=202 of these teachers) is paywalled (Springer 303s to an IdP login; not in Europe PMC) and its abstract-level description names the 17-item UWES, not the UWES-9 -- so the one accessible clue points at a DIFFERENT version than the dictionary assumes. Assigning any wording to Eng1..Eng9 would stack three guesses: instrument, version, and item order. (4) RIGHTS, INDEPENDENTLY. If it is a UWES, the wording could only be copied from the rights holders' own copy, which states: "The use is free for academic purposes only, such as PhD theses and scientific papers. For all other purposes, a contract should be drafted." (wilmarschaufeli.nl/downloads/, retrieved 2026-09-04), and the UWES Preliminary Manual repeats on each instrument page "(c) Schaufeli & Bakker (2003). The Utrecht Work Engagement Scale is free for use for non-commercial scientific research. Commercial and/or non-scientific use is prohibited, unless previous written permission is granted by the authors." That is a quotable, rights-holder-stated non-commercial restriction and itemtext_standard.md's 2026-09-04 ruling (irw#1891) fires exactly as it did for dominguez_2018_uwes in batch_027. The ECR-R source-licence carve-out has nothing to attach to here, because -- unlike a CC BY paper that itself printed the items -- this study's CC BY deposit publishes no wording at all. (5) Step 3b: no instrument-mismatch correction is possible or claimed; the live data is a 9-item, 1-7 self-report block whose identity the source never states.
